# Commands

<!-- Generated by pnpm run docs:generate. Edit the implementation, then regenerate both audiences. -->

These are the commands the doodlebot plugin adds. In Claude Code, type the command followed by its arguments; in Codex, choose the skill of the same name from the skill picker. See [Install the plugin](../get-started/install.md). This page is generated from each command's skill file.

## Set up and run the test Vortex

Install the companion, sign in, and start, stop or check the test copy of Vortex.

| Command               | What it does                                                                                                                                                                         | Arguments                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `/doodlebot:setup`    | Install or repair the doodlebot workspace, its doodlebot command and a sandbox baseline on this machine; use once per machine, or when another command says doodlebot is not set up. | <code>[folder] [--ref &lt;tag or branch&gt;] [--bin-dir &lt;folder&gt;]</code>                                                             |
| `/doodlebot:login`    | Sign the test Vortex in to Nexus Mods once and cache the login; use before working with Nexus collections, never for local checks.                                                   | <code>[--installed &#124; --dev-dir &lt;checkout&gt;]</code>                                                                               |
| `/doodlebot:baseline` | Create or refresh a baseline profile for the sandbox, a copy of a real game, or a source build; use when fresh starts should begin from a new clean state.                           | <code>[sandbox &#124; &lt;game id&gt; &lt;game folder&gt; &#124; source &lt;checkout&gt;]</code>                                           |
| `/doodlebot:start`    | Start the isolated test Vortex for an installed or source build with the sandbox, the Bethesda sandbox or a real game copy; use before driving or testing Vortex by hand.            | <code>[installed &#124; source &lt;checkout&gt;] [sandbox &#124; bethesda-sandbox &#124; &lt;game id&gt; &lt;game copy&gt;] [fresh]</code> |
| `/doodlebot:stop`     | Stop the running test Vortex cleanly; use when you are done, before starting another profile, or before tests, builds and updates.                                                   | none                                                                                                                                       |
| `/doodlebot:status`   | Report whether doodlebot is set up, whether the test Vortex is running and signed in, and whether its baseline exists; use when asked if doodlebot is ready.                         | <code>[doctor] [same target flags as start]</code>                                                                                         |
| `/doodlebot:update`   | Update the doodlebot workspace to match this plugin's version, then reinstall and rebuild it; use when another command reports a version mismatch.                                   | <code>[--ref &lt;tag or branch&gt;]</code>                                                                                                 |
| `/doodlebot:source`   | Clone and build the person's Vortex fork in the workspace and make a branch for one piece of work; use before changing Vortex's own code.                                            | <code>[branch name] [--update]</code>                                                                                                      |

## Work on Vortex

Fix, design, drive and check Vortex changes, and prepare their pull requests.

| Command              | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                               | Arguments                                                                                         |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/doodlebot:design`  | Design a Vortex or doodlebot feature or refactor with the Elephant-Goldfish Model before any code is written; use when a task adds a feature, refactors code, or the person supplies or asks for a design. | <code>&lt;feature or refactor request&gt;</code>                                                  |
| `/doodlebot:fix`     | Reproduce a Vortex bug on the base, fix it on a branch of the source checkout and verify the reported scenario with evidence; use for a bug report or broken Vortex behavior.                              | <code>&lt;bug report, issue link or symptom&gt;</code>                                            |
| `/doodlebot:drive`   | Drive the test Vortex through its UI (look, click, type, install, deploy, screenshot) and, for a scenario, return a run report; use to check a Vortex flow, reproduce a UI bug or demo a change.           | <code>&lt;what to do in Vortex, e.g. install this mod, deploy, and report anything odd&gt;</code> |
| `/doodlebot:qa`      | Run independent QA of a Vortex change from a fresh profile against its acceptance criteria and return a run report; use after the author has finished and stopped the test Vortex.                         | <code>&lt;change, branch or design&gt; [acceptance criteria]</code>                               |
| `/doodlebot:ui-test` | Write or debug a Playwright regression test for Vortex's UI in the doodlebot workspace and run it with doodlebot test core; use to lock in a UI behavior or fix a failing spec.                            | <code>&lt;UI behavior to test, or the failing spec&gt;</code>                                     |
| `/doodlebot:pr`      | Prepare a Vortex pull request: run the preflight checks, write the description with the doodlebot footer and check the PR's CI; use when a fix or feature is verified and ready to submit.                 | <code>[branch or checkout] [PR number, once it exists]</code>                                     |

## Benchmark

Measure Vortex performance and compare two Vortex builds.

| Command              | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Arguments                                                                                                 |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/doodlebot:measure` | Measure one Vortex build on one of doodlebot's performance checks, run several times, and report each metric's median and range; use for questions like how fast is the Mods table with 3,000 mods.              | <code>&lt;what to measure&gt; [on &lt;build&gt;]</code>                                                   |
| `/doodlebot:compare` | Compare two Vortex builds on one of doodlebot's performance checks, run alternately five times each, and report medians, ranges and a rule-based verdict; use for questions like is my branch slower than 2.8.0. | <code>&lt;build A&gt; &lt;build B&gt; &lt;what to measure, e.g. the Mods table with 3,000 mods&gt;</code> |
